question: What does the clock speed of a CPU measure?

options.text: The number of instructions executed per second
The amount of data processed per second

solution:
The correct answer is __The number of instructions executed per second__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Clock speed__ is a measure of how quickly a CPU can execute instructions.
 
• It is typically measured in Hertz (Hz), with modern CPUs operating in gigahertz (GHz).
 
• The higher the clock speed, the more instructions the CPU can process per second.
 
• However, performance also depends on factors like core count, architecture, and cache memory.
 
• Clock speed is an essential metric but not the sole determinant of CPU performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Count:**
 
 
• Modern CPUs often have multiple cores, allowing them to process multiple instructions simultaneously.
 
• This enhances performance for multitasking and parallel processing tasks.
 
 
 
• **Cache Memory:**
 
 
• Cache memory is a small, high-speed memory located inside the CPU.
 
• It stores frequently used instructions and data for quick access, reducing latency.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Management:**
 
 
• High clock speeds generate more heat, requiring efficient cooling systems.
 
• Thermal throttling can occur if the CPU overheats, reducing performance.
